This is for the open map, where we can see a clear and direct path that goes just outside the boundary of the person.  Increasing the repulsion strength made no difference, increasing the caused it to get stuck, increasing and decreasing the refinement step made no difference.
mission_3.comparison: All six of the trials succeeded. For A*, social_2 had the largest minimum person clearance, 0.731, vs 0.715 at baseline, and reduced_personal_space_s from 1.6s to 1.3s without costing time or distance. For RRT, social_1 had the largest clearance with a personal_space_s at 0 in every condition, it was also slightly faster and shorter. In both cases the wider spacing did not cost extra time or distance. The planned length and planning time were identical across conditions, so these small differences probably reflect execution variation from a single seed rather than a real effect.
mission_3.recommendation:
I would keep RRT social_1, it succeeded, had a 1.739m clearance, time of 43.242s, and distance of 11.499m. In comparison to A* social_2, it keeps a lot more distance from the person, spends no time in the threshold, and is faster and shorter. The tradeoff is that its minimum static clearance is only 0.14m, against about 0.63m for A*, so it passes much closer to walls, which could be a little worrisome for the robot, but since we are prioritizing space around a person I would still go with RRT. 

These static-person trials can't show how the robot handles people who move and have actual human functions where they change directions unpredictably and approach in different speeds. There is no information that tells us if the robot can react in time to that or if the actual people even feel safe or comfortable with the distance/spacing from the robot.
